flawed_step: Line 0024 (the "Distributing" step): from ((m\/n)\/b) /\ ((n\/m)\/a) \in F the proof concludes (m\/n) /\ (b\/a) \in F. The distributive law actually gives (x\/b) /\ (x\/a) = x \/ (b/\a) with x = m\/n, i.e. (m\/n) \/ (a/\b), not (m\/n) /\ (a\/b). Line 0027 ('b\/a \in M') is likewise unjustified; the intended hypothesis is a/\b \in M.
counterexample:
Take the 4-element Boolean lattice S = {0, p, q, 1} with p/\q = 0, p/q = 1 (distributive). Let F = {1} (an up-set closed under meet, hence a filter) and M = {0, p} (down-closed, closed under join, hence an ideal, disjoint from F; any strictly larger ideal must contain q, hence p/q = 1 \in F, so M is maximal disjoint from F). Put a = b = q and m = n = p \in M. Then m/a = p/q = 1 \in F and n/b = 1 \in F, so the proof's setup holds. Its chain up to line 0020 is fine: (m/n)/b = 1 \in F, (m/n)/a = 1 \in F, and their meet is 1 \in F. But the claimed 'distributed' form at line 0024 is (m/n)/\(b/a) = p/\q = 0, and 0 
otin F, so line 0024 is false. The correct distribution gives (m/n)/(a/ ) = p/0 = p, and indeed p 
otin F is consistent. Line 0027 also fails here: b/a = q 
otin M = {0,p}. (As a pure identity check, the simplest instance is the chain {0,1} with x = m/n = 1, a = b = 0: (x/b)/\(x/a) = 1 but x/\(b/a) = 1/\0 = 0.)
reasoning_summary: The proof's engine is the step at line 0024. Applying distributivity to ((m\/n)\/b) /\ ((m\/n)\/a) yields (m\/n) \/ (a/\b), not (m\/n) /\ (a\/b) as written. The rest of the argument depends entirely on this misapplied identity plus the unstated (and generally false) claim b\/a \in M at line 0027; in the correct version one uses the omitted hypothesis a/\b \in M so that (m\/n) \/ (a/\b) \in M contradicts disjointness from F. An explicit instance in the 4-element Boolean lattice (F = {1}, M = {0,p}, m = n = p, a = b = q) satisfies every hypothesis the proof uses, makes the line 0020 element equal 1 \in F, yet makes the line 0024 element equal 0 \notin F, refuting the step directly.
